text:
Elias Lindholm scored four goals on Saturday, and the Bruins needed every one of them. Boston beat Washington 7-5 in a game where the Capitals had the better chances, more shots and a goaltender who couldn't stop enough of them. Washington is now winless in five (0-5-0).

It was chaos from the start. Tom Wilson opened the scoring on a shot our numbers gave under a 1% chance, Lindholm tipped in a power-play tying goal, and Alex Tuch scored shorthanded. Boston took over early in the second: David Pastrnak tied it, Tanner Jeannot tipped in a go-ahead goal, and Lindholm made it 4-2, with Jeremy Swayman picking up an assist. The Capitals answered with Pierre-Luc Dubois on the power play and Dylan Strome's poke to tie it 4-4, a goal Ty Anderson of 98.5 The Sports Hub pinned on Casey Mittelstadt getting caught at the end of a long shift. Lindholm's deflection with 1:36 left in the second put Boston back ahead for good, and his snap shot early in the third made it 6-4.

The process favored Washington. The Capitals had 4.48 expected goals (the quality of their chances) to Boston's 4.01, outshot the Bruins 35 to 23, and drew 2.23 expected goals in the third period alone. Our replays gave Washington the win 75% of the time. The difference was in net: Charlie Lindgren allowed 3.2 goals more than his 22 shots deserved, while Swayman stopped Tuch on a 45% chance in the third with the Capitals pressing. Anderson wrote at 4-2 that he would have pulled Lindgren. Washington kept him in.

Jakob Chychrun's power-play goal, with Alex Ovechkin picking up an assist, made it 6-5 with 4:32 left, and Fraser Minten finished it late. Charlie McAvoy had three assists, as did Morgan Geekie, and Pastrnak had a goal and two.

Tom Gulitti noted it was Lindholm's third career hat trick and his first since Oct. 23, 2021, when he did it with Calgary, also against the Capitals. He took six shots worth 1.08 expected goals, so this wasn't all luck: he was getting to the right places. For Washington, five straight losses and a night like this one leave real questions about the goaltending, even with the chances going its way.
headline: Lindholm scores four as Bruins outlast the Capitals
